rows.name: Qur'an
rows.detail: Explicit basis: 65:6 (pay the wages), 28:26-27 ('hire him — the best you can hire is the strong and trustworthy'), 18:77 (a wage for the wall). Root a-j-r.
rows.detail_long: Three separate revelations legitimize hire: the command to pay nursing wages (65:6), Shu'ayb's daughter urging Musa's hiring (28:26-27), and Khidr's remark that a wage could have been taken for rebuilding the wall (18:77).

rows.timeline_year_basis: no app dating block — 610 period fallback
rows.name: Sunan Ibn Majah 2443
rows.detail: 'Give the worker his wages before his sweat dries.'
rows.detail_long: The wage-promptness command, graded Sahih in the app file — the ethical core of every hire contract.
rows.internal_ref: Record + grading pulled from app hadith file (kafalah_source_extract.json session)

rows.timeline_year_basis: no app dating block — 610 period fallback
rows.name: Sahih Bukhari 2227
rows.detail: Hadith qudsi: Allah will oppose on the Day of Resurrection 'one who employs a laborer, takes full work, and does not pay his wages.'
rows.detail_long: One of three persons Allah declares Himself against — the unpaid-labor prohibition that grounds the enforceability of wage claims.
rows.internal_ref: Record + grading pulled from app hadith file (kafalah_source_extract.json session)

rows.display_note: Shown at 622 CE; app dating range 622–622 CE, confidence high
rows.name: Sahih Bukhari 2263
rows.detail: The Prophet and Abu Bakr hired a pagan expert guide from Bani al-Dil for the Hijra — dated by the app to 622 CE, high confidence.
rows.detail_long: Aisha's narration: camels entrusted to the hired guide, rendezvous at the Cave of Thaur three days later. Hire across religious lines, on trust, at the community's most dangerous hour — and the app dates it to the Hijra year itself.
rows.internal_ref: Record + grading pulled from app hadith file (kafalah_source_extract.json session)

rows.name: al-Tabari
rows.detail: Al-Tabari on 28:26 and 65:6 establishes hire/wage legitimacy and conditions.
rows.detail_long: Al-Tabari on 28:26 (6,900 chars) and 65:6 (8,800 chars) in the app validates wage labor from both directions: Shu'ayb's daughter's 'hire him — the strong, the trustworthy' as the employer's criteria, and the command to pay nursing mothers their wages as the duty side.
rows.evidence_display: Jami' al-Bayan (Tafsir al-Tabari), on Q28:26 (text in app)
rows.internal_ref: Passage read verbatim this session from app tafsir file (batch2_source_extract.json)

rows.name: Fakhr al-Din Razi
rows.detail: Al-Razi's commentary adds the conditions analysis of hire.
rows.detail_long: Tafsir al-Kabir dissects what makes a hire valid — known work, known wage, capable worker — the analytic layer between scripture and fiqh manuals. App book F0575-B50 (no tafsir edition of Razi in the app's reader; book record only).
rows.internal_ref: saa.pdf p.4; figure + book confirmed in app

rows.name: Ibn Abbas (attrib., Tanwir al-Miqbas)
rows.detail: The earliest attributed gloss on 28:26 — 'Hire him! the best you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy.'
rows.detail_long: Tanwir al-Miqbas (in the app) on the Moses hiring verse: the strong 'who can bear a heavy load', the trustworthy 'regarding that with which you entrust him'. The Qur'an's own two-line job specification — competence plus integrity — glossed at the very start of the tafsir tradition. Attribution traditional, not critical — hence 'attrib.'
rows.evidence_display: Tanwir al-Miqbas (attrib. Ibn Abbas), on Q28:26 (text in app)
rows.internal_ref: Passage read verbatim from app tafsir file (batch3_source_extract.json, 2026-07-14)

rows.name: Mufti Muhammad Shafi Usmani
rows.detail: Ma'ariful Qur'an on 28:26: the two qualities every hire requires — strength for the work, trustworthiness with what is entrusted.
rows.detail_long: The app's Ma'ariful Qur'an passage on 28:26 (read this session): Shu'ayb's daughter argues the case for hiring Moses on exactly two grounds — 'he should be strong, and... he should be trustworthy'. The modern mufassir drawing the employment doctrine straight from the verse: capability plus amanah as the hiring test.
rows.evidence_display: Ma'ariful Qur'an, on Q28:26 (text in app)
rows.internal_ref: Passage read verbatim from app tafsir file (batch3_source_extract.json, 2026-07-14)

rows.name: Ibn Rushd
rows.detail: Comparative validation: all four schools accept ijarah by Qur'an, Sunnah and consensus; only Ibn al-Asamm rejected it.
rows.detail_long: Bidayat records near-unanimity on leasing — the lone dissent (Ibn al-Asamm, on uncertainty grounds) proving the rule. App book F0751-B51.
rows.internal_ref: saa.pdf p.4; figure + book confirmed in app

rows.name: Ibn Qudama al-Maqdisi
rows.detail: Al-Mughni vol. VI: the detailed Hanbali rulebook of leasing; Malikis/Hanbalis add the 'lawful benefits' limit.
rows.detail_long: The leasing book of al-Mughni covers usufruct definition, rent conditions and termination — with the Maliki-Hanbali restriction that only lawful benefits can be leased. App book F0749-B50.
rows.internal_ref: saa.pdf p.4; figure + book confirmed in app

rows.timeline_year_basis: adopted as rules 29-31 May 2000 (meeting 4); readopted as a Standard at meeting 8, 11-16 May 2002
rows.name: AAOIFI
rows.detail: AAOIFI Shari'ah Standard No. 9: ijarah + lease-ending-in-ownership (IMB) — engine of asset finance and ijarah sukuk.
rows.detail_long: SS9 codifies operating and financing leases plus ijarah muntahia bittamleek. VERIFIED: rules adopted 31 May 2000, reformatted as Standard 16 May 2002. CLAUSES VERIFIED-TO-TEXT THIS SESSION (SS9, ss1.txt): 3/1 the lease must be preceded by acquisition of the asset or its usufruct; 4/1/1 the lease is binding on both parties; 4/1/2 duration must be specified; 5/1/1 the leased asset must be usable while preserved and the benefit Shari'ah-permissible; 7/1/1 sale of the asset to the lessee terminates the ijarah; 8/1 in Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek the title transfer must sit in a document SEPARATE from the lease.
rows.evidence_display: AAOIFI Shari'ah Standard No. 9: ijarah + lease-ending-in-ownership (IMB)
rows.internal_ref: Verified from the official AAOIFI Shari'ah Standards 2015 full text (user-supplied PDF, adoption page read this session) | SS9 clauses read verbatim from ss1.txt (2026-07-14)

rows.name: Industry practice
rows.detail: Ijarah = 16.9% of 2022 sukuk issuance (IFSB 2023) — the core of asset finance.
rows.detail_long: Aircraft, real estate and equipment finance run on ijarah; it is the second-largest sukuk structure after wakala.
